us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
UNITED STATES POLICY

*   **Executive Order on Securing America's Defense Supply Chains:** On July 20, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to enhance the security of the U.S. defense supply chains. This order limits the circumstances under which the Secretary of Defense can issue waivers for critical materials sourced from covered nations, particularly requiring mitigation plans to onshore supply chains in certain cases. It also directs the Department of War to initiate regulatory action for more comprehensive supply chain mapping and encourages defense contractors to qualify new domestic and partner nation sources for critical minerals, materials, and components, while removing regulatory barriers. Previously, defense contractors could more easily obtain waivers to source critical materials from prohibited foreign suppliers, including China, if it was deemed the easiest or cheapest option. Now, companies seeking a waiver must demonstrate a thorough search for alternatives, disclose material origins, and provide a plan to transition away from prohibited suppliers, facing potential contract loss for non-compliance. This action aims to reduce reliance on overseas supply chains, particularly from geopolitical adversaries, for crucial defense equipment.

*   **Proclamations Imposing Additional Section 338 Tariffs on Canada:** On July 20, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed three separate proclamations imposing additional 50% tariffs on approximately $20 billion in imports from Canada under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930. These tariffs target Canadian motor vehicles, alcoholic beverages, and dairy products, effective August 19, 2026, to offset Canada's discriminatory treatment of U.S. commerce in these sectors. Previously, the U.S. had ongoing trade disputes with Canada, but these specific 50% tariffs under Section 338, a statute not previously used to impose tariffs, are new. The tariffs will not apply to energy, potash, Section 232 tariffs, fish, or critical minerals. This action escalates trade tensions with Canada, aiming to correct perceived imbalances and ensure fair treatment for American exports.

*   **CFTC Sunsets Routine Large Trader Reporting Requirements for Physical Commodity Swaps:** On July 20, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) issued a final order sunsetting the routine position-reporting requirements of Part 20, the large trader reporting rules for physical commodity swaps. This means clearing organizations, clearing members, and swap dealers are no longer required to file daily and event-based position reports under Part 20. Previously, these entities were mandated to provide daily position data to the CFTC to facilitate surveillance of physical commodity swaps. The CFTC determined that the information collected through these reports is now largely available via its matured swap data reporting regime, though it retains the authority under § 20.6 to request underlying records and futures-equivalent conversion methods on special call. This change streamlines reporting obligations for market participants while maintaining regulatory oversight.

*   **FTC Settlement with Celsius Network Founders:** On July 20, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced a settlement with Alexander Mashinsky, former CEO of Celsius Network Inc., and business partners Shlomi Daniel Leon and Hanoch “Nuke” Goldstein, requiring them to pay a total of $16.5 million. The settlement resolves FTC charges that they deceived users by falsely promising easy withdrawals, a $750 million insurance policy, sufficient reserves, and high annual percentage yields for deposits. The founders are also prohibited from marketing or selling products or services that allow the deposit or withdrawal of certain assets, making misrepresentations about product benefits, and violating the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. This enforcement action aims to compensate consumers who suffered losses due to the deceptive practices of the cryptocurrency platform.

*   **FTC Settlement with Caremark Rx LLC and Zinc Health Services LLC:** On July 14, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced a settlement with Caremark Rx LLC and Zinc Health Services LLC (Caremark) in an administrative antitrust case against the nation's largest pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs). Under the settlement, Caremark agreed to structural changes in its pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement practices, including ceasing discrimination against lower-cost drug versions on standard drug coverage lists, providing a standard offering that bases members' out-of-pocket expenses on the drug's net cost, and capping out-of-pocket insulin costs through affordability programs. The FTC estimates this settlement will generate up to $8.5 billion in consumer savings over 10 years and an additional $4.5 billion from point-of-sale rebates. Previously, Caremark's practices allegedly limited competition and increased drug costs through various pricing and reimbursement methods. This action mandates significant changes to PBM practices to increase transparency and reduce drug costs for consumers.

Why it matters: The U.S. government has significantly escalated its trade enforcement actions against Canada with new tariffs while simultaneously tightening defense supply chain regulations and continuing to enforce consumer protection and antitrust measures.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **U.S.-Iran Conflict:** The United States conducted its ninth consecutive night of airstrikes against Iran early Monday, targeting suspected underground missile bases, following the death of a third U.S. service member in Iraq on Saturday from a downed Iranian drone. In retaliation, Iran launched attacks on Bahrain, the home of the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet, and Kuwait, also striking a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. This escalation has led to a near halt in shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed Brent crude prices above $90 a barrel on Monday. The intensifying conflict poses a significant threat to global energy supplies and could destabilize international trade routes, impacting the world economy. [Al Jazeera, AP, Reuters]

• **United Kingdom:** Andy Burnham officially became Britain's new Prime Minister on Monday, July 20, accepting King Charles III's invitation to form a government after the resignation of his predecessor. In his inaugural speech from Downing Street, Burnham pledged to introduce a "new political model and a new economic model," aiming to re-industrialize Britain and bring essential services under stronger public control, marking a reversal of policies from the 1980s. His immediate plans include unveiling measures to address the cost of living crisis and a comprehensive 10-year national strategy later this week. This leadership change in a G7 economy, coupled with a promise of fundamental policy shifts, could significantly alter international alliances, trade relations, and the global economic landscape. [AP, Al Jazeera, GOV.UK]

• **China (Artificial Intelligence):** Chinese technology companies showcased hundreds of advanced robotics and artificial intelligence systems at the World AI Conference in Shanghai, which concluded on July 20. The annual event emphasized China's accelerated progress in AI development amidst a backdrop of strategic competition with the United States. This demonstration highlights China's intensified efforts towards technological self-reliance and its ambition for global leadership in cutting-edge fields like AI and robotics. China's rapid advancements in these sectors carry strategic implications for global technological dominance, economic competition, and national security, influencing future industrial and military capabilities worldwide. [AP]

• **Aerospace Industry:** GE Aerospace, in collaboration with NASA, BETA Technologies, and Boeing, announced on July 20 at the Farnborough International Airshow the successful completion of the aviation industry's first hybrid electric flight above 30,000 feet. This milestone demonstrated the viability of fully integrated megawatt-class and multi-kilovolt hybrid electric propulsion systems, with one flight in hybrid electric mode lasting over two hours. This breakthrough significantly advances the development of more electric aircraft engine systems, promising enhanced efficiency, durability, and range for future aviation. The development is a critical step towards more sustainable air travel, potentially reducing the industry's carbon footprint and establishing new global standards for aircraft design and fuel efficiency. [GE Aerospace]

• **Democratic Republic of Congo / Uganda (Ebola Outbreak):** The Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen to at least 930 people, including dozens of healthcare workers, with 1,963 confirmed infections in the DRC and 20 cases in neighboring Uganda as of mid-July. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency in May, but ongoing armed conflict in eastern DRC, particularly affecting the Kigonze displacement camp where 20,000 people reside, is severely hindering containment efforts. Germany has responded by increasing its support for the fight against the outbreak, committing an additional 13 million euros to assist affected populations and countries. The unchecked spread of Ebola in a conflict-ridden region represents a grave humanitarian crisis and a significant global health risk, underscoring the formidable challenges of disease control amidst instability and insufficient resources. [AP, Deutsche Welle]

Why it matters: The confluence of escalating geopolitical conflicts, significant political transitions in major economies, and rapid technological advancements is creating a highly uncertain and volatile global landscape, while simultaneously highlighting critical humanitarian and environmental challenges.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Apoio Social a Pessoas com Deficiência:** A Lei n.º 31/2026, de 14 de julho, alarga e torna gratuito o Serviço de Assistência Pessoal (MAVI) para pessoas com deficiência ou incapacidade. Anteriormente, poderia haver comparticipações familiares ou verificação de recursos; agora, o acesso é totalmente gratuito. O Governo tem como meta expandir este serviço em 30% no primeiro ano de execução através da celebração de novos acordos e do aumento de horas de assistência. O impacto prático é uma melhoria significativa no apoio e na autonomia das pessoas com deficiência, eliminando barreiras financeiras e aumentando a disponibilidade do serviço.

• **Novo Modelo de Ação Social no Ensino Superior:** O Decreto-Lei n.º 148/2026, de 20 de julho, estabelece um novo modelo para a política de ação social escolar no ensino superior, revogando legislação anterior como o Decreto-Lei n.º 129/93 e a Lei n.º 8/2025. Este diploma garante que o custo do alojamento para estudantes bolseiros é totalmente coberto, ao invés de depender de apoios insuficientes, e obriga as instituições de ensino superior a oferecerem serviços de apoio psicológico e a adaptarem os seus serviços a estudantes com necessidades educativas específicas. O impacto prático é uma redução da carga financeira para estudantes bolseiros com despesas de alojamento e um reforço crucial do apoio à saúde mental e à inclusão de todos os estudantes.

• **Licenciamento de Matadouros Móveis:** O Decreto-Lei n.º 147/2026, de 20 de julho, regulamenta o licenciamento e o funcionamento de matadouros móveis e estabelecimentos móveis de manipulação de caça em Portugal Continental. Anteriormente, pequenos produtores rurais e caçadores enfrentavam custos e stress significativos com o transporte de animais vivos ou carcaças para matadouros fixos distantes. A nova lei permite que o abate e o processamento ocorram mais perto da origem, minimizando o transporte. O impacto prático é a redução de custos e de stress animal para pequenos produtores e o fomento da economia rural através de circuitos de comercialização mais curtos e eficientes.

Why it matters: As novas medidas visam melhorar diretamente a qualidade de vida e o acesso a serviços essenciais para pessoas com deficiência e estudantes universitários, ao mesmo tempo que modernizam e apoiam as atividades económicas rurais.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **New EU Air Passenger Rights Regulation:** Airlines, intermediaries, and booking platforms are now required to offer free seating for children under 14 next to their parents or guardians, and for pregnant individuals and those with reduced mobility next to their companions. Previously, these seats often incurred reservation fees. Additionally, airlines must correct name spellings on tickets free of charge, provide printed boarding passes without extra cost, and display airfares including cabin baggage by default. Previously, these services could be subject to fees or less transparent pricing. Passengers who miss the outbound leg of a return ticket will now be able to take the return flight without penalty, a change from previous "no-show" clauses that could cancel the entire booking. Clearer compensation rules for disrupted travel are also introduced, with passengers having up to nine months to file claims. These new rules will enter into force in mid-2027, approximately 12 months and 20 days after their publication in the Official Journal. This significantly enhances consumer protection for air travellers and requires airlines and booking platforms to adapt their pricing and service policies.

• **EU Cloud and AI Development Act:** This new rulebook, published in the Official Journal on July 15, 2026, imposes concrete obligations on cloud service providers and AI product builders operating within the EU. Previously, there were less prescriptive rules regarding data sovereignty and supply chain transparency in these sectors. Now, companies must adhere to enhanced requirements concerning data locality, public sector procurement of cloud services, increased documentation, transparency, and stricter scrutiny of their supply chains. This aims to fortify EU-based AI infrastructure and reduce reliance on non-EU providers. This regulation significantly impacts tech companies, increasing compliance burdens, but also fosters a more robust and independent European digital market.

• **Listing Act Directive (EU) 2024/2811 – Infringement Procedure:** The European Commission launched infringement procedures on July 15, 2026, by sending a letter of formal notice to Portugal and 17 other Member States for failing to fully transpose the Listing Act Directive into national law by the June 5, 2026, deadline. Previously, investment firms were subject to stricter MiFID II rules on paying for research. This Directive aims to make EU public capital markets more attractive, especially for smaller companies, by improving access to capital and fostering financial research. The new rules offer investment firms greater flexibility in how they pay for third-party research and clarify the regulatory perimeter for issuer-sponsored research. Portugal's failure to transpose means Portuguese businesses and investors cannot yet fully benefit from these simplified capital market rules, and the country faces potential sanctions if it does not comply within two months.

• **Revised Single Permit Directive (EU) 2024/1233 – Infringement Procedure:** The European Commission initiated infringement procedures on July 15, 2026, against Portugal and 16 other Member States for not fully transposing the revised Single Permit Directive into national law by the May 21, 2026, deadline. Previously, non-EU workers in Member States were often tied to a single employer, and application processing times could be up to 120 days. The new Directive strengthens the EU framework for labour migration by allowing non-EU workers to change jobs, employers, and work sectors under certain conditions (via notification to authorities), and shortens the decision deadline for single permit applications from 120 to 90 days. It also permits applications from third countries or from within the EU for those already holding a valid residence permit. Portugal's non-compliance means businesses hiring non-EU workers and the workers themselves in Portugal are not yet benefitting from these updated, more flexible rules, and the country faces legal action.

Why it matters: This week saw significant steps towards consolidating EU regulatory power in digital and financial markets through new legislation and robust enforcement actions, notably highlighting Member States' obligations in transposing key economic and social directives.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **DeepSeek V4:** DeepSeek officially launched its V4 model, including Pro and Flash versions, with a 1-million-token context window across both. DeepSeek V4-Pro, with 1.6 trillion total parameters (49B activated), reportedly achieved 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified, positioning its performance near Claude Opus 4.6 but at approximately one-seventh the output API price, while introducing a new peak and off-peak API pricing structure. Developers can now leverage a highly capable and cost-effective open-weight model for complex coding, mathematical reasoning, and agent-based task execution, enabling significant cost reductions for intensive AI workloads.

• **Adobe Project Indigo:** Adobe released an experimental AI Playground feature within its Project Indigo iOS camera app. This update integrates real-time photo critiques, automated object removal, depth-of-field generation, and stylistic edits, driven by Google's Nano Banana model and offering button-driven, deterministic controls. Mobile photographers can receive immediate, AI-powered feedback on composition and lighting before capturing a shot, and effortlessly execute advanced editing tasks like removing distractions through guided interactions.

• **NVIDIA Cosmos3-Edge:** NVIDIA released Cosmos3-Edge, a 4-billion parameter open-source model available on Hugging Face. This model is specifically designed for Physical AI applications such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart space environments, and is licensed under OpenMDW1.1 for global deployment. Researchers and developers in hardware-centric AI fields can now access a specialized and openly licensed model to accelerate the development and testing of robust physical AI solutions.

Why it matters: The continuous rollout of highly specialized and cost-optimized AI models, coupled with advanced AI features integrated into consumer productivity tools, reflects a deepening maturity in the AI landscape, making cutting-edge capabilities more accessible and practical for diverse real-world applications.
